Package hadur2.core.move

Class BulletShadows

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.move.BulletShadows
public final class BulletShadows extends Object
MOVE-1: where our bullets shadow an enemy wave. The engine moves each bullet along a straight segment every turn and destroys two bullets whose segments cross that turn. The enemy's bullet lies on a ray from the wave's source, between the wave's radii at the turn's start and end, so it meets our bullet's segment exactly when its firing angle is the bearing (from the source) of a point of that segment inside the ring those two radii bound. The union of those bearings over the turns both bullets fly is the shadow: a bullet the enemy fired at any of them dies before it reaches us.

Shadows are bearings from the wave's source, in radians (Robocode's compass: 0 north, clockwise), not guess factors: the surf scores bearings anyway, and a bearing interval needs no assumption about the enemy's escape angle. Two lists come out, following the engine's order of play (see cast): the certain shadow, angles whose bullet meets one of ours whatever order the engine moves the two in, and the possible shadow, which adds the angles that meet in only one of the two orders. Wave stores both and its shadowedFraction counts a possible shadow as half, so the surf keeps 1 - (certain + possible / 2) of a wave's danger at an intersection.

MoveController.updateShadows(long) calls of(hadur2.core.model.Wave, java.util.List<hadur2.core.move.OurBullet>, double, double) for each enemy firing wave when the wave is new or our bullets in flight have changed. The work is bounded (RES-2): at most MAX_TURNS turns per bullet, and a bullet is followed only while it is on the field. The class is stateless.

  • Field Details

    • MAX_TURNS

      static final int MAX_TURNS
      Turns followed at most per bullet. At the slowest bullet speed, 11 px a turn, that is 1,320 px, more than the 1,000 px diagonal of the standard 800 x 600 field; a bullet that leaves the field sooner stops the walk sooner.

    • ring

      static void ring(Point2D.Double s, Point2D.Double a, Point2D.Double b, double inner, double outer, List<double[]> out)
      Adds the bearings from s of the points of segment a-b whose distance from s is in [inner, outer].

      With the segment written P(t) = a + t (b - a) for t in [0, 1], the squared distance |P(t) - s|^2 is the quadratic qa t^2 + qb t + qc. It is at most outer^2 between the roots of qa t^2 + qb t + qc - outer^2, and under inner^2 strictly between the roots of the inner one, so the part in the ring is at most two sub-segments: [lo, hi] less the inner interval. At most two intervals are added.

      Parameters:
      s - the centre, the wave's source
      a - the segment's start
      b - the segment's end
      inner - the ring's inner radius, in px (0 on the wave's first turn)
      outer - the ring's outer radius, in px
      out - receives [low, high] bearing intervals, in radians

    • merge

      static List<double[]> merge(List<double[]> raw)
      Merges overlapping intervals; angles are made continuous around the first one.

      Each interval's low end is moved by whole turns to within pi of the first interval's low end, keeping its width; the intervals are then sorted and swept once, joining any that overlap or touch. This assumes all of a wave's shadows lie within half a turn of each other.

      Parameters:
      raw - the intervals; returned as is when empty
      Returns:
      a new list of disjoint [low, high] intervals sorted by low
